reports.title: Anaptys Reports Fiscal First Quarter 2027 Financial Results and

lines: Anaptys continues to expect to achieve >$390 million in annualized Jemperli royalties payable to Anaptys as early as 2029 at GSK’s peak monotherapy sales guidance of >$2.7 billion2

Anaptys estimates Sagard will have accrued ~$330 million in royalties and sales milestones through September 30, 2026 and anticipates paydown of the remaining ~$270 million non-recourse debt monetization in calendar H2 2027

desk.headline: Revenue down 60% to $30.3m after last year's milestone; EPS of $0.11 misses estimates; Jemperli royalty target kept

other.label: G&A expense
other.change: vs $1.1m a year ago; incl. $4.8m litigation costs

results: Revenue fell to $30.3m from $76.3m because last year's quarter included a $50m milestone; Jemperli royalties rose 11% from the previous quarter.
Net income was $3.9m ($0.11 a diluted share), held down by $18.7m of non-cash interest on the royalty sale to Sagard.
Costs rose as the GSK/Tesaro lawsuit cost $4.8m; G&A was $11.6m against $1.1m a year ago.
GSK reported Jemperli sales of $365m for the quarter, up 20%, and the drug was approved in the US for some rectal cancers.
Cash and investments fell by $11.1m to $153.0m.

guidance.summary: Anaptys gives no revenue or earnings guidance. It still expects Jemperli royalties of more than $390m a year as early as 2029 and expects to finish repaying the Sagard royalty deal (about $270m left) in the second half of 2027.

watch: The Delaware court ruling in the GSK/Tesaro case, expected in Q4 2026 or Q1 2027; Anaptys wants Jemperli rights returned.
The FDA decision on Quimilza (imsidolimab) for generalised pustular psoriasis, due 12 Dec 2026.
Jemperli sales growth and legal costs.
